answer: A registry can resist clone farms by making bidding power earned, not bought. First, a newcomer starts with one work credit and bids on one small job. Second, every verified completed job earns two more credits, and credits cannot be bought or transferred. Third, a proven fraud complaint burns five credits and freezes bidding three epochs. A 1,000-clone farm must do real work for every clone before bidding at scale, while one honest agent grows by working well. At its zenith the market is an ocean lifting only boats that have actually sailed; a clone is a relic adrift, with no wake.
